newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong stocks in London nudge lower on caution.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks in London nudge lower on caution.

text.p: Hong Kong shares trading in London edged lower on Friday in thin, cautious trade ahead of the weekend and a decision on U.S. interest rate policy next week.
Investors were also fretting over talk that Beijing was planning tough measures to cool down the over-heated stock markets.

The Hang Seng London Reference Index was down 4.59 points at 14,057.78 by 1413 GMT. In Hong Kong on Friday the Hang Seng gained 20.47 points or 0.15 percent to finish above the key 14,000 level after spending much of the day in negative territory.

"The gain in Hong Kong overnight was small and there's caution in the market surrounding the China shares," said one dealer. "Talk that China may bring in some anti-speculation measures which will affect China shares that trade in Hong Kong," he added.
"People are also cautious ahead of the FOMC meeting on Tuesday and we've hardly seen any turnover at all ahead of the weekend," the trader said.
Shares in HSBC were trading at HK$219 in London, HK$1 off their Hong Kong close.

"In Hong Kong we've closed just above the 14,000 level again and we're likely to see a bit of consolidation until after the figures on Tuesday...but then we may continue to push ahead," one dealer said.
